svg.title: Cross-encoder repeats label encoding per document; a bi-encoder caches it
svg.desc: A cross-encoder jointly re-encodes labels with every document, so throughput collapses as the label list grows. A bi-encoder encodes labels and text separately so the label embeddings can be pre-computed once and reused, turning the label side of inference into a cache read. At 1,024 entity types, the pre-computed bi-encoder loses only 5.2% throughput versus a single label, while the cross-encoder loses 98.7%.

svg.text: Cache the labels, not just the text
